# Mobi POS Codebase Dossier

Generated from the current workspace on 2026-09-17. This file is a readable source snapshot plus a concise architecture guide.

## Scope

Included: application source, Rust/Tauri source, shared packages, workers, scripts, schemas, configuration, standards, documentation, and text assets.

Excluded: `node_modules`, `target`, build output, generated Android build intermediates, databases, images/binaries, archives, source maps, local `.env` files, and this dossier itself.

The worktree had pre-existing modified and untracked files when this dossier was generated; no existing file was reverted or normalized.

## System Overview

Mobi POS is a Tauri 2 desktop/mobile point-of-sale application. The user interface is React + TypeScript, packaged for desktop and Android/iOS through Tauri. Local checkout is designed to work offline using SQLite, while Turso Cloud stores merchant data and exchanges changes through a custom synchronization layer.

### Main Components

- **UI shell:** `src/App.tsx`, `src/components`, `src/hooks`, and `src/store` provide checkout, catalog, customer, repair, procurement, reporting, settings, mobile companion, and modal workflows.
- **State and domain:** Zustand slices in `src/store/slices`, domain commands/reducers in `src/domain`, business utilities in `src/utils`, and shared types/schemas in `src/types`, `src/schemas`, and `packages/shared`.
- **Local persistence:** `src/db` and `src/db/sqlPluginAdapter.ts` use Tauri SQLite through `@tauri-apps/plugin-sql`; Dexie is used as a browser/UI mirror or fallback.
- **Synchronization:** `src/sync/SyncManager.ts` drains the local `sync_outbox` to Turso with idempotent batch upserts, pulls remote rows using cursors, and uses HLC/event-log support for convergence experiments.
- **Cloud transport:** `src/sync/tursoClient.ts` uses `@libsql/client` for direct Turso access. `workers/relay` provides Cloudflare Durable Object WebSocket signaling so peers know when to pull.
- **Native shell:** `src-tauri` contains Tauri commands, migrations, capabilities, keychain integration, printing, reducers, HLC code, and platform packaging.
- **Rust core crates:** `crates/pos-core` contains portable POS models, money math, errors, and the `PosDb` abstraction; `crates/pos-peripherals` contains peripheral integration boundaries.
- **Cloud schema and operations:** `turso/remote-schema.sql`, `scripts`, `docs`, and ADRs define schema rollout, migrations, recovery, sync diagnostics, release gates, and operational procedures.

### Data Flow

```text
Cashier / companion UI
        |
        v
Zustand slices -> DB adapters -> local SQLite transaction
                                  |
                                  +--> domain rows + inventory/ledger rows
                                  +--> sync_outbox / event_log
                                               |
                         SyncManager + @libsql/client batch push
                                               v
                                      Turso Cloud database
                                               ^
                                               |
                         cursor/HLC pull + local projection/reducer
                                               ^
Cloudflare relay: signal only, then peer pulls data from Turso
```

### Important Current Sync Model

The current implementation is application-level logical synchronization, not Turso native CDC-powered sync. It uses a local transactional outbox, custom batch writes, cursor/HLC pulls, and relay notifications. Turso native sync would require a local synced database engine and a controlled migration away from this transport.

## Source Snapshot

### `.github/workflows/five-target-ci.yml`

```yaml
name: Five-Target CI Matrix (Desktop + Mobile)

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  quality-gates:
    name: Lint, Types & Business Invariant Tests
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup Node.js 20
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Typecheck & Lint
        run: |
          npm run lint
          npx tsc -b

      - name: Run Automated Test Suite (113 Invariants)
        run: npm test

  build-desktop:
    name: Desktop Build (${{ matrix.platform }})
    needs: quality-gates
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - platform: Windows
            os: windows-latest
            target: x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
          - platform: macOS
            os: macos-13
            target: x86_64-apple-darwin
          - platform: Linux
            os: ubuntu-22.04
            target: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install Linux Dependencies
        if: matrix.platform == 'Linux'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev libappindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev patchelf libudev-dev

      - name: Setup Rust Stable
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          targets: ${{ matrix.target }}

      - name: Install npm dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Build Web Assets
        run: npm run build

      - name: Compile Tauri Binary (Check Only)
        run: cargo check --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml --target ${{ matrix.target }}

  build-mobile:
    name: Mobile Build Check (${{ matrix.target }})
    needs: quality-gates
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - target: aarch64-linux-android
            os: ubuntu-22.04
          - target: aarch64-apple-ios
            os: macos-14
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Setup Rust Stable
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          targets: ${{ matrix.target }}

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Setup Android NDK
        if: matrix.target == 'aarch64-linux-android'
        run: |
          ANDROID_HOME=/usr/local/lib/android/sdk
          NDK_VERSION=$(ls -1 $ANDROID_HOME/ndk 2>/dev/null | sort -V | tail -n 1)
          if [ -z "$NDK_VERSION" ]; then
            echo "Installing NDK..."
            yes | $ANDROID_HOME/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager "ndk;26.1.10909125"
            NDK_VERSION="26.1.10909125"
          fi
          NDK_PATH="$ANDROID_HOME/ndk/$NDK_VERSION"
          echo "Found Android NDK at: $NDK_PATH"
          echo "ANDROID_HOME=$ANDROID_HOME" >> $GITHUB_ENV
          echo "NDK_HOME=$NDK_PATH" >> $GITHUB_ENV
          echo "$NDK_PATH/toolchains/llvm/prebuilt/linux-x86_64/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH
          echo "CC_aarch64_linux_android=$NDK_PATH/toolchains/llvm/prebuilt/linux-x86_64/bin/aarch64-linux-android24-clang" >> $GITHUB_ENV
          echo "AR_aarch64_linux_android=$NDK_PATH/toolchains/llvm/prebuilt/linux-x86_64/bin/llvm-ar" >> $GITHUB_ENV

      - name: Compile Mobile Target (Cargo Check)
        run: cargo check --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml --lib --target ${{ matrix.target }}
```

### `.github/workflows/release.yml`

```yaml
name: Release Tauri App (Multi-Platform Matrix)

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - 'v*'
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  test-and-lint:
    name: Pre-Release Quality Gates
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Install Dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Run Linter & Typecheck
        run: |
          npm run lint
          npx tsc -b

      - name: Run Automated Invariant Tests
        run: |
          npm test
          node src/utils/runLoyaltyTests.cjs
          node src/utils/runSystemTests.cjs

  build-tauri:
    name: Build & Package (${{ matrix.platform }})
    needs: test-and-lint
    permissions:
      contents: write
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - platform: 'windows-latest'
            target: 'x86_64-pc-windows-msvc'
            args: ''
          - platform: 'macos-latest'
            target: 'universal-apple-darwin'
            args: '--target universal-apple-darwin'
          - platform: 'ubuntu-22.04'
            target: 'x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu'
            args: ''

    runs-on: ${{ matrix.platform }}

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install System Dependencies (Linux)
        if: matrix.platform == 'ubuntu-22.04'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev libappindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev patchelf libudev-dev

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Setup Rust Stable
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          targets: ${{ matrix.platform == 'macos-latest' && 'aarch64-apple-darwin,x86_64-apple-darwin' || '' }}

      - name: Rust Cache
        uses: swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: './src-tauri -> target'

      - name: Install frontend dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Build and Publish Tauri Release
        uses: tauri-apps/tauri-action@v0
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD }}
        with:
          tagName: ${{ github.ref_name }}
          releaseName: 'MobiPOS ${{ github.ref_name }}'
          releaseBody: 'MobiPOS Release ${{ github.ref_name }}. Includes production bug fixes, performance optimizations, and security updates.'
          releaseDraft: false
          prerelease: false
          includeUpdaterJson: true
          args: ${{ matrix.args }}

  build-android:
    name: Build & Package Android APK
    needs: [test-and-lint, build-tauri]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Setup Java 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'

      - name: Setup Android Environment & NDK
        run: |
          echo "ANDROID_HOME=/usr/local/lib/android/sdk" >> $GITHUB_ENV
          export ANDROID_HOME=/usr/local/lib/android/sdk
          if [ -d "$ANDROID_HOME/ndk/26.1.10909125" ]; then
            echo "NDK 26.1.10909125 already available."
          else
            echo "Installing NDK 26.1.10909125..."
            yes | $ANDROID_HOME/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager "ndk;26.1.10909125"
          fi
          echo "NDK_HOME=$ANDROID_HOME/ndk/26.1.10909125" >> $GITHUB_ENV

      - name: Setup Rust Stable
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          targets: 'aarch64-linux-android,armv7-linux-androideabi,i686-linux-android,x86_64-linux-android'

      - name: Install frontend dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Build Web Assets
        run: npm run build

      - name: Build Android APK
        env:
          NDK_HOME: /usr/local/lib/android/sdk/ndk/26.1.10909125
        run: |
          npx tauri android build --apk

      - name: Prepare & Sign Android APKs
        run: |
          mkdir -p release-assets/android
          # Locate built APKs
          APK_FILES=$(find src-tauri/gen/android/app/build/outputs/apk -name "*.apk" -type f)
          echo "Found built APKs:"
          echo "$APK_FILES"

          # Pick universal or release APK
          UNIVERSAL_APK=$(echo "$APK_FILES" | grep -i "universal.*release" | head -n 1 || echo "$APK_FILES" | grep -i "release" | head -n 1 || echo "$APK_FILES" | head -n 1)

          if [ -n "$UNIVERSAL_APK" ] && [ -f "$UNIVERSAL_APK" ]; then
            echo "Processing primary APK: $UNIVERSAL_APK"
            TAG="${{ github.ref_name }}"

            # Check if APK is unsigned; if so, create a release keystore and sign it
            if [[ "$UNIVERSAL_APK" == *"unsigned"* ]]; then
              echo "Signing release APK..."
              keytool -genkey -v -keystore release.keystore -alias mobipos -keyalg RSA -keysize 2048 -validity 10000 \
                -dname "CN=MobiPOS, OU=POS, O=Mobi, L=Algiers, S=Algiers, C=DZ" -storepass mobipos123 -keypass mobipos123

              $ANDROID_HOME/build-tools/34.0.0/apksigner sign --ks release.keystore --ks-pass pass:mobipos123 \
                --key-pass pass:mobipos123 --out release-assets/android/MobiPOS-Android.apk "$UNIVERSAL_APK"
            else
              cp "$UNIVERSAL_APK" release-assets/android/MobiPOS-Android.apk
            fi

            cp release-assets/android/MobiPOS-Android.apk "release-assets/android/MobiPOS-${TAG}-android.apk"
            echo "Generated release APKs in release-assets/android/:"
            ls -lh release-assets/android/
          else
            echo "::error::No release APK found in build outputs!"
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Upload Android APKs to GitHub Release
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2
        if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/')
        with:
          files: |
            release-assets/android/MobiPOS-Android.apk
            release-assets/android/MobiPOS-*-android.apk
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      # Manual runs (workflow_dispatch): no tag => no Release, so publish the
      # APKs as run artifacts instead. Zero local setup needed to get a test
      # APK: Actions tab -> Release Tauri App -> Run workflow -> download artifact.
      - name: Upload Android APKs as Run Artifact (manual runs)
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: ${{ !startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/') }}
        with:
          name: MobiPOS-Android-APK
          path: release-assets/android/*.apk
          if-no-files-found: warn

  build-ios:
    name: Build & Package iOS App (IPA)
    needs: [test-and-lint, build-tauri]
    runs-on: macos-14
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
          cache: 'npm'

      - name: Setup Rust Stable
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          targets: 'aarch64-apple-ios,aarch64-apple-ios-sim,x86_64-apple-ios'

      - name: Install frontend dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Build Web Assets
        run: npm run build

      - name: Initialize iOS Project (if not generated)
        run: |
          if [ ! -d "src-tauri/gen/apple" ]; then
            echo "Initializing iOS Xcode project..."
            npx tauri ios init
          else
            echo "iOS project already initialized in src-tauri/gen/apple"
          fi

      - name: Compile iOS Target
        run: |
          # Build iOS target without codesigning requirement for direct sideloading (AltStore, Sideloadly, TrollStore)
          npx tauri ios build --debug --target aarch64-apple-ios || true

      - name: Package iOS IPA
        run: |
          mkdir -p release-assets/ios
          TAG="${{ github.ref_name }}"

          APP_DIR=$(find ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData src-tauri -name "*.app" -type d 2>/dev/null | head -n 1 || true)

          if [ -n "$APP_DIR" ] && [ -d "$APP_DIR" ]; then
            echo "Found iOS App bundle: $APP_DIR"
            mkdir -p payload_dir/Payload
            cp -r "$APP_DIR" payload_dir/Payload/
            cd payload_dir
            zip -r ../release-assets/ios/MobiPOS-iOS.ipa Payload
            cd ..
            rm -rf payload_dir
            cp release-assets/ios/MobiPOS-iOS.ipa "release-assets/ios/MobiPOS-${TAG}-ios.ipa"
            echo "Successfully created IPA: release-assets/ios/MobiPOS-iOS.ipa"
            ls -lh release-assets/ios/
          else
            echo "Warning: .app directory not found directly. Creating iOS source archive fallback."
            cd src-tauri
            tar -czf ../release-assets/ios/MobiPOS-iOS-source.tar.gz gen/apple 2>/dev/null || tar -czf ../release-assets/ios/MobiPOS-iOS-source.tar.gz Cargo.toml
            cd ..
          fi

      - name: Upload iOS Assets to GitHub Release
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2
        if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/')
        with:
          files: |
            release-assets/ios/*
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
```

### `AGENTS.md`

```markdown
# AGENTS.md â€” Autonomous Engineering Charter Â· Tauri v2 POS

**Version:** 1.0 Â· **Issued:** 2026-09-14 Â· **Audience:** the autonomous coding agent working this repository (any agent that reads root instruction files â€” Codex, Cursor, Copilot coding agent, Claude Code, etc.).
**Companion spec:** `docs/TAURI_V2_POS_PLAYBOOK.md` (v2.0) â€” the engineering constitution: stack, architecture, sync design, edge-case compendium, budgets, distribution. This charter is your operating license and standing orders, not a replacement for it.
**Precedence:** playbook > this charter > agent improvisation. Where they disagree, follow the playbook and file a discrepancy note (Â§8.2) â€” never silently pick a side.
**Conventions:** `MUST` = non-negotiable Â· `SHOULD` = strong default Â· âŒ/âœ… = forbidden/required.

---

## Â§0 â€” Orientation: the 60-second read

You are the autonomous engineer of a production point-of-sale system: **one Tauri v2 + Vue 3 codebase shipped to five targets (Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, iOS), offline-first at the till, with real-time Turso cloud sync â€” a desktop sale visible on the phone in â‰¤ 1.5 s p95.** Merchants run this software to take money every day. That fact shapes every rule below.

Your mandate has two halves, and both are the job:

1. **Build** â€” implement the roadmap (Â§7) to the playbook's standards, through the operating loop (Â§4), passing the gates (Â§6).
2. **Discover** â€” when a gap, a doubt, or a better tool exists, hunt it down across GitHub and the wider web, verify it against primary sources, and integrate or reject it with recorded reasons (Â§5). Waiting to be told what to search for is a failure mode, not humility.

You are measured against six contracts. They are numbers, not aspirations:

| # | Contract | Value | Where enforced |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | Sync latency: desktop sale â†’ phone visible | â‰¤ 1.5 s p95 | CI two-device suite (playbook Â§7.5) |
| C2 | Checkout with network fully down | 100 % of sale paths | offline chaos suite (playbook Â§10.2) |
| C3 | Cold start â†’ first interactive | â‰¤ 900 ms desktop SSD Â· â‰¤ 1.8 s Android mid Â· **â‰¤ 3.0 s Android-low floor** Â· â‰¤ 1.5 s old iOS | perf gate blocks the tag (playbook Â§11.1) |
| C4 | Merchant install friction | one artifact, zero external dependencies, first sale â‰¤ 90 s | release checklist (playbook Â§12 + its App. B) |
| C5 | Duplicate-charge tolerance | zero â€” every mutation carries an idempotency key | replay tests (playbook Â§6.6) |
| C6 | Silent data loss | zero â€” outbox invariant + boot recovery before reads are served | fresh-chain CI tests (playbook Â§5.4) |

If a change you are about to make would break a contract number, stop and escalate (Â§8.3). If you don't know whether it does, you haven't read the playbook section that governs it â€” route via Appendix B.

**Read order on day one:** this file (all of it) â†’ playbook Â§0 (ten decisions) â†’ Â§1 (repo shape) â†’ the phase you're assigned in Â§7 â†’ the playbook sections Appendix B routes you to. Never work from memory of "how Tauri/Turso usually works" â€” Â§2 Rule ZERO and Â§5 apply.

---

## Â§1 â€” Mission & system shape

**What you are building.** A register that keeps selling when the internet dies, a companion app in the owner's pocket that shows the day live, and a cloud spine that makes the business's data survive any single till being dropped in a bucket of water. SQLite on the terminal is the source of truth for the terminal; Turso (one database per merchant) is the source of truth for the business. The UI never writes to both. Sync is a background concern and never a checkout gate.

```
â”Œâ”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€ ONE REPO Â· FIVE TARGETS â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”
â”‚  Vue 3 UI â”€â”€invoke()â”€â”€â–¶ Rust commands â”€â”€â–¶ pos-core      â”‚
â”‚  (reads local       â—€â”€â”€db:changedâ”€â”€     (SQLite, WAL)   â”‚
â”‚   replica only)                          push()/pull()  â”‚
â””â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”¬â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”€â”˜
            TURSO CLOUD â—€â”€â”€â”˜ (one DB per merchant, PITR)
                 â–² signal "when" (wss://)      â””â”€ data "what"
        SIGNAL RELAY â€” Cloudflare Worker + Durable Object /merchant-room
```

**The ten decisions, already made â€” do not relitigate, do not re-derive** (full rationale: playbook Â§0.2):

| # | Decision | Locked value |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Framework | Tauri v2 only â€” one repo, five targets. âŒ No Capacitor / RN / Flutter |
| 2 | UI | Vue 3 (`<script setup>` + TS), platform-adaptive (POS mode / companion mode) |
| 3 | SQL home | All SQL lives in Rust (`crates/pos-core`) â€” the webview has no Node, no `fs`, no native SQLite |
| 4 | Sync engine | `turso` crate (`--features sync`) = Engine A; `libsql` embedded replicas = Engine B â€” both behind one `PosDb` trait (playbook Â§6.1) |
| 5 | âŒ `tauri-plugin-sql` | forbidden for synced tables (no replication protocol) â€” local scratch only |
| 6 | Real-time | Signal relay (CF Worker + DO rooms) carries *when*; `pull()` carries *what*; epoch-guarded |
| 7 | Schema | Built for sync: ULID keys, `updated_at` + `device_id`, soft deletes, append-only money tables, idempotency keys |
| 8 | Durability | Assume the OS can kill the process at any instruction: WAL, outbox, boot recovery (playbook Â§6.6) |
| 9 | Performance | Cold-start budgets per device class, tested on the worst device supported (Android Go) |
| 10 | Delivery | One zero-dependency artifact per platform; stores are the mobile channel |

---

## Â§2 â€” The law you build under

**Rule ZERO (read before any sync-layer work).** Turso's sync surface is young and moves fast. Before writing sync code, re-check `docs.turso.tech/sync/usage` and `crates.io/crates/turso` for the current API and mobile-target support. Never invent method names â€” copy them from current docs and record them in the ADR. This rule generalizes (Â§5.4): **your memory of any API is a hypothesis; the docs are the experiment.**

**The five sentences (playbook Â§0.3, binding):**

1. **The till keeps selling offline.** Every sale path works with the network down.
2. **SQLite is the source of truth for the terminal; Turso for the business.** The UI never writes to both.
3. **Every mutation carries an idempotency key.** Retries are guaranteed; duplicates are a choice.
4. **Least privilege in capabilities, secrets in the OS keychain, validation at every boundary.**
5. **If it isn't in CI, it doesn't exist.** Builds, tests, migrations, budgets, releases â€” all machine-enforced.

**Stack baseline you may assume without re-verifying** (verified Sept 2026; re-verify yearly, playbook Â§0.1 holds the source trail):

| Component | Assume | Watch out |
|---|---|---|
| Tauri | 2.x stable (~2.9.x), mobile stable since 2.0 | Re-check floors before release |
| Vue | 3.5.x stable, Pinia 4.x, VueUse 14.x | âŒ 3.6/Vapor is RC â€” do not ship |
| Vite | 8.x (Rolldown default) | Build floor â‰ˆ Chrome 87 / Safari 13 = webview floor |
| TypeScript | 6.0.x | âŒ 7.0 native port not yet vetted for vue-tsc |
| Tailwind | 4.3.x CSS-first (`@theme`) | No `tailwind.config.js` |
| Mobile floors | Android 7 / SDK 24 Â· iOS 13 | WKWebView enforces CORS â€” no bypass exists |
| Turso Engine A | `turso` crate â€” `push()`/`pull()`/`checkpoint()`, CDC, Turso Sync GA | API moves â€” Rule ZERO |
| Data fetching | `@tanstack/vue-query` v5 | Cache invalidation driven by `db:changed` events |
| Peripherals | `escpos-rs`+TCP 9100/`nusb`, `serialport-rs` â€” desktop-gated | playbook Â§14.1 |
| Validation | `garde` (Rust) Â· `zod/v4-mini` or `valibot` (TS, exactly one) | playbook Â§14.6 |

**âŒ Standing rejections (adopting any of these is a charter violation, not a style choice):** React for the shell (superseded) Â· Supabase as backbone (superseded) Â· `tauri-plugin-sql` on synced tables Â· `tauri-plugin-turso` / Drizzle-on-libsql in the webview (JS-side SQL = drift bug class) Â· Turso Multi-DB Schemas (deprecated for new users) Â· `bwip-js` in the webview Â· plain-`zod` whole bundle Â· floats for money Â· `moment`/`lodash` (use `Intl` + ES APIs) Â· native-module JS clients in the webview (NAPI can't load there) Â· card data anywhere in our code (PCI scope stays zero).

---

## Â§3 â€” Repository protocol

```
pos/
â”œâ”€â”€ apps/shell/                  # the ONE Tauri app (five targets)
â”‚   â”œâ”€â”€ src/routes/              # route-level code splitting (playbook Â§11.3)
â”‚   â”œâ”€â”€ src/features/            # checkout/ orders/ catalog/ sync/ settings â€” no cross-imports
â”‚   â”œâ”€â”€ src/platform/            # ONLY place allowed to import @tauri-apps/* (playbook Â§2)
â”‚   â””â”€â”€ src-tauri/{commands/, sync/, capabilities/, gen/android, gen/ios}
â”œâ”€â”€ crates/pos-core/             # domain + DB + sync engine â€” ZERO tauri::* imports
â”œâ”€â”€ crates/pos-peripherals/      # printing/scanning/scales â€” #[cfg(desktop)] gated
â”œâ”€â”€ packages/shared/             # TS types mirroring Rust DTOs + zod schemas
â”œâ”€â”€ workers/relay/               # Cloudflare Worker + Durable Object (playbook Â§7.2)
â””â”€â”€ docs/adr/                    # NNNN-slug.md â€” every non-trivial decision
```

**Placement laws (MUST):**

- Business logic (totals, tax, voids, stock math) lives in `pos-core`, compiled into every target, tested headlessly with `cargo test`. A domain rule that only exists inside a Tauri command cannot be unit-tested and drifts between platforms.
- The webview talks to Rust only through the `platform/` seam and the typed `invokeCommand` wrapper (playbook Â§4.1). A stray `invoke()` anywhere else is a review-blocking defect.
- `gen/android` and `gen/ios` are **generated but owned**: committed, and edits to them are deliberate (mobile plugin code rides there â€” playbook Â§14.2), never accidental regeneration.
- Lockfiles committed (pnpm + Cargo) Â· `rust-toolchain.toml` pins ONE stable Rust, enforced identically in CI Â· TS `strict: true` + `noUncheckedIndexedAccess: true`.
- Capabilities are per-platform (`desktop.json` / `mobile.json`), minimal, and reviewed like credentials. âŒ Never widen a capability to make something work â€” that "fix" is a security incident deferred.

**ADR discipline.** Any decision that is expensive to reverse, touches sync, schema, or the IPC surface, or adopts/rejects a dependency gets an ADR: `docs/adr/NNNN-slug.md` with *Context Â· Options Â· Decision (with measurements) Â· Consequences*. Dependencies adopted without an ADR get reverted on sight.

---

## Â§4 â€” Your operating loop

Run this loop for **every** task, no matter how small. Skipping steps is how silent errors are born â€” and silent errors are the worst class in this system (playbook Â§9.3).

```
ORIENT   â†’ read this charter's relevant Â§ + the playbook sections Appendix B routes you to
PLAN     â†’ smallest reversible slice; if a decision is involved, draft the ADR first
DISCOVER â†’ if any gap/doubt exists, run the Â§5 engine BEFORE coding
BUILD    â†’ to the playbook's standards for that layer (Â§3/Â§4/Â§5 of the playbook)
VERIFY   â†’ run every gate in Â§6 that the diff can touch â€” locally, before the PR
RECORD   â†’ ADR if decided Â· ledger row if discovered Â· changelog if user-visible
```

### 4.1 Autonomy ladder â€” what you may do without asking

| Level | Scope | Autonomy |
|---|---|---|
| L0 | Read, research, run tests, run Â§5 discovery | **Fully autonomous** â€” do this constantly |
| L1 | Implement to the playbook inside the existing architecture: code, tests, migrations, CI wiring, bug fixes | **Fully autonomous** â€” PR + self-review (Â§6.2) |
| L2 | Adopt a NEW dependency or plugin that passes the Â§5 scorecard and the âŒ list in Â§2 | **Autonomous with record** â€” scorecard + benchmark + ADR in the same PR |
| L3 | Architecture or contract changes: engine swap, schema migration on synced tables, SLO/budget change, capability widening, adding a platform | **Blocked on human approval.** Prepare the ADR + impact analysis + migration plan, then stop and escalate (Â§8.3) |

You are *empowered* to L2 without asking â€” that is the point of this charter. What you are never empowered to do is L3 quietly, or L2 without the record.

### 4.2 Anti-hallucination tripwires (each of these is a firing offense in a codebase that takes money)

- âŒ **Never invent an API.** No crate method, Tauri command, config key, or SQL pragma enters the codebase from memory. Copy from current docs (Â§5.4) and cite the source in the PR/ADR.
- âŒ **Never claim a test passed that you did not run.** "Should pass" is a status report about your imagination, not the code.
- âŒ **Never mark a migration applied without checking `PRAGMA user_version`** on a real DB file.
- âŒ **Never widen a capability, CSP directive, or permission to unblock yourself.**
- âŒ **Never commit secrets, tokens, or the updater private key.** DSNs and tokens arrive at runtime via vendor config / OS keychain.
- âŒ **Never swallow an error** to make a path green. A swallowed `Result` in this system is a future line item in a merchant's books.
- âŒ **Never present unverified version claims as facts** â€” version-sensitive statements carry a source date or they don't exist (Â§5.4).

### 4.3 Commits, PRs, and the universal Definition of Done

- Conventional Commits (`feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:` â€¦); one logical change per PR; PRs stay small enough to review honestly (~â‰¤ 400 lines diff as the ceiling, not the target).
- A task is **done** when, in the same PR: (1) `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` + `cargo test --workspace` + `pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test` all green â€” actually run, not assumed; (2) tests for the new behavior exist and assert the failure mode, not just the happy path; (3) contracts C1â€“C6 are unchanged, or the escalation was filed (Â§8.3); (4) an ADR exists if a decision was made; (5) performance-touching diffs carry measured numbers (before/after); (6) playbook cross-references in your docs still resolve; (7) the PR passes the Â§6.2 self-review checklist.

---

## Â§5 â€” The Skill-Discovery Engine (your standing order)

This section is not permission â€” it is obligation. The playbook's Â§14 was produced by exactly this engine (4 rounds, 41 queries, every finding integrated or rejected with reasons), and it must keep running through you. **A quarter in which you hit none of the Â§5.2 triggers and ran no discovery pass is a failed quarter**: crates go unmaintained, Turso and Tauri surfaces move, and a stale dependency list is worse than none.

### 5.1 What discovery is for

Three goods, in order: (1) **close gaps** â€” anything the playbook doesn't name (v1.0 had no printing stack, no search strategy, no monitoring, no payments posture â€” playbook Â§14 closed them); (2) **kill doubt** â€” any "I think this is the current API/version/behavior" feeling becomes a verified fact or gets corrected; (3) **find leverage** â€” a tool, pattern, or technique that makes a contract number (C1â€“C6) cheaper to hit.

### 5.2 Mandatory triggers â€” run discovery when any of these fire

| Trigger | Response |
|---|---|
| You are starting a phase or feature the playbook doesn't fully specify | Gap-list â†’ Â§5.3 queries â†’ findings note before coding |
| The same error or wrong behavior happens twice | Search the exact error + repo (GitHub issues of the crate/plugin) before attempt #3 |
| A version/platform/behavior claim can't be cited to a dated primary source | Rule ZERO generalized: verify or discard â€” never code from memory |
| A dependency in the graph goes > 6 months without a release or shows advisories | Re-evaluate: `cargo audit`, `npm audit`, repo activity â€” swap or pin with an ADR |
| Pre-minor-release checkpoint (quarterly cadence) | Full pass over the gap radar (Â§5.7) + stack baseline re-verification |
| A vendor ships something on the radar (e.g., Turso server-push) | Spike it; if it lands, propose the ADR that retires what it replaces |

### 5.3 The search kit â€” how to hunt

Query discipline first: **gap-specific queries, not generic "best library" fishing.** "escpos rust crate USB 2026" beats "rust receipt printing library". Search like an engineer who knows exactly what's missing.

```bash
# GitHub â€” repos, code, and the issues of a specific dependency
gh search repos "tauri pos" --sort=updated --limit=20
gh search repos --topic=tauri --topic=escpos
gh search code "PosDb" --language=rust          # how others solved the same seam
gh api search/issues -f q='repo:tauri-apps/tauri barcode-scanner ios'
gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/releases/latest      # is it alive? what changed?

# Ecosystem registries â€” recency and download health
cargo search escpos && cargo search turso        # then crates.io for deps/rust_version/last_updated
npm search @tauri-apps --json                    # then bundlephobia for gzip size

# Wider web â€” official docs outrank everything
#   docs.turso.tech Â· tauri.app/plugins Â· crates.io Â· bundlephobia.com
#   awesome-tauri (the maintained list) Â· hn.algolia.com (adoption signal, pitfalls in comments)
#   r/tauri Â· SQLite docs (sqlite.org/fts5.html) Â· vendor changelogs/release notes

# Supply-chain & health checks before adoption
cargo audit && cargo outdated && cargo bloat     # advisories, staleness, binary cost
pnpm audit && pnpm dlx npm-check-updates        # same for the webview side
```

### 5.4 The verification protocol â€” believe nothing secondhand

- **Primary sources only:** official docs, the crate/npm page itself, the repo's own README/issues/releases. Blog posts and AI answers are leads, never evidence.
- **Every version- or platform-sensitive claim carries a source and a date** â€” e.g. "tauri-plugin-barcode-scanner: iOS âŒ (official plugin docs, checked 2026-09)". Undated claims don't go in ADRs, PRs, or the ledger.
- **Test the claim where cheap:** a 10-line `cargo` spike beats a 10-paragraph Stack Overflow answer. Numbers or it didn't happen.
- **Record findings** in `research/` (raw) and the findings note (distilled) â€” the playbook's `research/t6_*.json` + `scripts/research_task6_r*.sh` pattern is the template: scripted, archived, re-runnable.

### 5.5 The evaluation scorecard â€” every candidate, before adoption

| Criterion | Pass condition | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Maintenance | Commit/release activity â‰¤ 6 months Â· issues triaged, not composting | A graveyard with good docs is still a graveyard |
| License | MIT / Apache-2.0 / ISC only | âŒ GPL-family and unfree licenses poison a commercial POS |
| Correctness evidence | Tests, changelog discipline, real-world usage signals | Sentry-plugin-class libs need named production users |
| Dependency footprint | Rust: pure, no C build chain (playbook Â§12 zero-dep rule) Â· webview: bytes accounted against playbook Â§11.3 budgets | `nusb` over libusb for exactly this reason |
| Security | `cargo audit`/`npm audit` clean Â· no advisory history that repeats | Check before every adopt AND every re-verify |
| Platform matrix | Compiles for aarch64-linux-android + aarch64-apple-ios, not just desktop | Phase-0-style spike is the only proof |
| Law fit | Violates nothing in Â§2 â€” esp. SQL-in-Rust, webview purity, money-as-integer | A brilliant law-breaking lib is still rejected |

**Verdict rules:** *Adopt* (integration spec + roadmap slot + ledger row) Â· *Defer* (named re-evaluation trigger â€” "defer" without a trigger is a no) Â· *Reject* (one-line reason in the ledger). No link dumps â€” a finding that enters the repo without a decision is debt wearing a discovery costume.

### 5.6 The integration pipeline â€” from finding to shipped

1. **Spike** on a scratch branch; compile for all five targets (mobile emulators count for matrix proof).
2. **Benchmark against the current approach** â€” startup delta, sync p95, bundle/binary bytes. Numbers in the ADR or it didn't happen.
3. **ADR + ledger row + roadmap slot** in one PR (L2 autonomy, Â§4.1).
4. **Capability & CSP audit** â€” new plugins get their permissions reviewed like credentials, then wired into per-platform capability files (playbook Â§1.4).
5. **CI wiring** â€” golden tests where the finding is testable (the `escpresso` virtual-printer pattern: receipts asserted as bytes, not vibes).

### 5.7 The standing gap radar â€” each row is a live bounty

Hunt these deliberately; strike rows when closed, add rows when felt:

| Radar item | Why it's open | Status / trigger |
|---|---|---|
| **Turso server-push notifications** | Would retire the signal relay (playbook Â§7) | Does not exist (verified 2026-09) â€” re-check every quarter |
| Partial / lazy sync in the `turso` crate | Big-catalog merchants pay full-pull cost | Experimental TS/Py/Go only â€” re-check Rust support |
| iOS camera scanning | Official barcode plugin is Android-only | Native AVFoundation/ML Kit plugin slated Phase 5; `zxing-js` fallback meanwhile |
| Android USB printing | `escpos-rw`/`nusb` are desktop-gated | Deliberate later plugin â€” needs USB-host mode reality check |
| CJK product search | Trigram tokenizer is weak below 3-char terms | Phase-6 spike (2-gram tokenizer or ICU) if a CJK market lands |
| iOS silent push for background sync | OS throttles background work (Doze/silent-push) | Evaluate with real data in Phase 6, not vibes |
| Stripe Terminal desktop | Native mobile plugin is the v1 path | JS SDK + smart reader only if demand justifies the CSP surface |
| `tauri-plugin-autostart` Windows bug | Registry entry can vanish after one boot (GitHub, Nov 2023) | Track upstream; re-assert-on-boot mitigation already the rule |
| Vue 3.6 / Vapor Mode | RC, unstable | Watch GA + `vue-tsc` support; adopt via scorecard, never early |
| Engine B offline-writes maturity | `libsql` historical beta status | Re-check if Engine A falters; `PosDb` trait makes it a spike, not a rewrite |

### 5.8 Forbidden hunts â€” do not spend cycles here

The âŒ list in Â§2 is final for this codebase; re-proposing `tauri-plugin-sql` for synced tables or a webview ORM is not "discovery", it's relitigating settled law. Escape hatches (`cr-sqlite`, Evolu, PowerSync, ElectricSQL) are **documented deferrals** with named triggers â€” re-evaluate only when those triggers fire.

## Â§6 â€” Engineering gates (what "verified" means)

### 6.1 The gate matrix â€” run locally before every PR, enforced in CI

| Gate | Command | Blocks |
|---|---|---|
| Rust quality | `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings && cargo test --workspace` | every PR |
| Rust security | `cargo audit` | dependency-touching PRs |
| Frontend quality | `pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test` | every PR |
| Sync contract | `pnpm test:e2e:sync` (two-device suite, relay ON + relay-kill â†’ poll convergence) | sync-touching PRs |
| Offline contract | airplane-mode checkout chaos suite (nightly, debug build) | release |
| Performance | budgets â†’ `perf-report.json` â€” Android-low cold start regression > 10 % fails | release tags |
| Receipts | `escpresso` golden-bytes assertions (line count, total, cut, drawer-kick after cash tender only) | peripheral-touching PRs |
| Five-target build | CI matrix: win / macos / linux / android (JDK 17, NDK) / ios (macos runner) | release |

### 6.2 PR self-review checklist (paste into every PR description, tick honestly)

- [ ] Contracts C1â€“C6 unchanged, or escalation filed (Â§8.3)
- [ ] All Â§6.1 gates relevant to this diff actually run, locally
- [ ] New/changed behavior has tests asserting the failure mode
- [ ] Money paths: integer minor units end-to-end, `rust_decimal` only for intermediate math
- [ ] No `unwrap()`/`expect()` outside tests; no swallowed `Result`s
- [ ] Errors map to the taxonomy (`PosError` codes), never stringly-typed
- [ ] All SQL in `pos-core`; no `invoke()` outside the `platform/` seam; no new capability entries unless ADR'd
- [ ] Migrations append-only, fresh-chain tested from empty DB
- [ ] New deps: scorecard + benchmark + ADR + ledger row attached
- [ ] Bundle/binary size deltas measured; > 10 KB gzip needs one-line justification
- [ ] Playbook cross-refs in touched docs still resolve

## Â§7 â€” Roadmap & acceptance (correctness before latency)

Work phases **in order** â€” a fast-but-wrong dashboard is worse than a slow-but-right one; the merchant trusts the number, not the badge. Full table: playbook Â§13.

| Phase | Goal | Definition of done |
|---|---|---|
| **0. Spike & restructure** | `PosDb` trait; both Turso engines compile + sync on emulators; engine ADR | ADR-001 with measurements |
| **1. Mobile shells green** | Five-target CI; bootstrap script | New contributor reaches `android dev` from README alone |
| **2. Read-only companion** | Pull-only mobile; boot recovery; honest sync badge | Desktop checkout â†’ companion â‰¤ 2 s with relay OFF |
| **3. Live** | Relay + DO rooms; epoch guard; `db:changed` invalidation; sync-health panel | C1 met on CI two-device suite; relay-kill â†’ converge â‰¤ 35 s |
| **4. Offline writes** | Outbox flusher; idempotent replay; conflict policy in core | Airplane-mode chaos green; duplicate-replay green |
| **5. Ship** | Stores, signing, staged rollout, Sentry, perf gate, runbooks | AAB + IPA approved; updater verified; first merchant live â‰¤ 90 s |
| **6. Harden & measure** | Device-matrix quarterly; discovery cadence; radar strikes | Zero p95 regressions two quarters running |

Per-phase extras: Phase 2 lands FTS5 search (migration 0003) and desktop keyboard-wedge scanning; Phase 4 lands the peripherals crate (printing, drawer, scales); Phase 5 lands Sentry + exports + autostart-with-mitigation; Phase 6 is where radar rows become spikes. Slot details: playbook Â§14.10 ledger.

## Â§8 â€” Failure & escalation protocol

### 8.1 The three-attempt rule (being stuck is a state to report, not hide)

After 3 failed attempts at the same error: **stop.** Write the stuck report in the PR/issue: exact error output, the last 3 commands, hypotheses attempted and why each failed, what Â§5.3 searches you ran and what they said. Escalate to the human with that bundle. Three silent retries after three failures is how a 20-minute fix becomes a corrupted local DB.

### 8.2 Discrepancy protocol (playbook vs reality)

When current, dated, primary-source reality contradicts the playbook: **follow reality**, then file a discrepancy note as a draft ADR tagging the playbook section â€” the playbook gets patched in the next PR. Reality never loses to documentation, and documentation never gets silently overridden.

### 8.3 Severity classes â€” what halts immediately

| Class | Examples | Action |
|---|---|---|
| ðŸ”´ **Halt** (data/money integrity) | WAL corruption, outbox loss, duplicate charge risk, card data touching our code, secrets in a diff | Stop work, revert risk, report to human within the hour |
| ðŸŸ  **Escalate** (contract) | Any C1â€“C6 regression, capability/CSP widening pressure, L3 change | ADR + impact analysis, block on approval |
| ðŸŸ¡ **Record** (quality) | Flaky test, budget drift < 10 %, ADR-needed refactor | Ledger/ADR entry in the normal flow |

### 8.4 When the human is unavailable

Keep working down the roadmap at L1/L2 Â· record everything Â· batch escalations into a single decision queue with your recommendation and the cost of each option Â· never let "nobody answered" become "I widened the capability".

### `build-android.bat`

```bat
@echo off
REM ==============================================================================
REM MobiPOS â€” One-Click Android APK Build (PC)
REM Double-click this file. It verifies AND auto-repairs the whole toolchain
REM (Java 17+, Android SDK packages, NDK, Rust targets), then builds an
REM install-ready DEBUG APK. No Android Studio needed.
REM
REM Release/signed APKs stay on CI: push a tag (v*) and GitHub builds them.
REM ==============================================================================
setlocal EnableDelayedExpansion
cd /d "%~dp0"

echo.
echo  ============================================================
echo   MobiPOS â€” Android APK builder (one click)
echo  ============================================================
echo.

REM ---------- [1/6] Node.js (required for the Tauri CLI) ----------
where node >nul 2>nul
if errorlevel 1 (
  echo [FATAL] Node.js not found. Install LTS from https://nodejs.org then re-run.
  pause
  exit /b 1
)
for /f "tokens=*" %%v in ('node -v') do echo [OK] Node %%v

REM ---------- [2/6] Java 17+ (required for Gradle) ----------
where java >nul 2>nul
if errorlevel 1 (
  echo [FATAL] Java not found. Install Temurin JDK 17: winget install EclipseAdoptium.Temurin.17.JDK
  pause
  exit /b 1
)
node scripts\check-java.mjs
if errorlevel 1 (
  echo        Install: winget install EclipseAdoptium.Temurin.17.JDK
  pause
  exit /b 1
)

REM ---------- [3/6] Rust Android targets ----------
where rustup >nul 2>nul
if errorlevel 1 (
  echo [FATAL] rustup not found. Install from https://rustup.rs then re-run.
  pause
  exit /b 1
)
echo [OK] rustup found â€” ensuring Android targets...
call rustup target add aarch64-linux-android armv7-linux-androideabi >nul 2>nul

REM ---------- [4/6] Locate Android SDK ----------
if not defined ANDROID_HOME (
  if exist "%LOCALAPPDATA%\Android\Sdk" set "ANDROID_HOME=%LOCALAPPDATA%\Android\Sdk"
)
if not defined ANDROID_HOME (
  echo [FATAL] ANDROID_HOME not set and no SDK at %%LOCALAPPDATA%%\Android\Sdk.
  echo        Install "Android SDK Command-line Tools" once, then set ANDROID_HOME.
  echo        See: https://developer.android.com/studio#command-line-tools-only
  pause
  exit /b 1
)
echo [OK] ANDROID_HOME=%ANDROID_HOME%

set "SDKMANAGER="
if exist "%ANDROID_HOME%\cmdline-tools\latest\bin\sdkmanager.bat" set "SDKMANAGER=%ANDROID_HOME%\cmdline-tools\latest\bin\sdkmanager.bat"
if not defined SDKMANAGER (
  if exist "%ANDROID_HOME%\cmdline-tools\bin\sdkmanager.bat" set "SDKMANAGER=%ANDROID_HOME%\cmdline-tools\bin\sdkmanager.bat"
)

REM ---------- [5/6] Auto-install missing SDK packages ----------
set "NEED_INSTALL=0"
if not exist "%ANDROID_HOME%\platform-tools\adb.exe" set "NEED_INSTALL=1"
if not exist "%ANDROID_HOME%\platforms\android-36" set "NEED_INSTALL=1"
if not exist "%ANDROID_HOME%\build-tools" set "NEED_INSTALL=1"

if "%NEED_INSTALL%"=="1" (
  if not defined SDKMANAGER (
    echo [FATAL] SDK packages missing and no sdkmanager found.
    echo        Install command-line tools into %%ANDROID_HOME%%\cmdline-tools\latest, then re-run.
    pause
    exit /b 1
  )
  echo [...] Installing missing SDK packages ^(platform-tools, android-36, build-tools^)...
  call "%SDKMANAGER%" --install "platform-tools" "platforms;android-36" "build-tools;35.0.0"
  if errorlevel 1 (
    echo [FATAL] sdkmanager failed. Run it once manually to accept licenses.
    pause
    exit /b 1
  )
) else (
  echo [OK] SDK packages present.
)

REM ---------- NDK (auto-detect newest, install default if absent) ----------
if not defined NDK_HOME (
  for /d %%d in ("%ANDROID_HOME%\ndk\*") do set "NDK_HOME=%%d"
)
if not defined NDK_HOME (
  if not defined SDKMANAGER (
    echo [FATAL] No NDK found and no sdkmanager to install one.
    pause
    exit /b 1
  )
  echo [...] Installing NDK 26.1.10909125 ^(matches CI^)...
  call "%SDKMANAGER%" --install "ndk;26.1.10909125"
  set "NDK_HOME=%ANDROID_HOME%\ndk\26.1.10909125"
)
echo [OK] NDK_HOME=%NDK_HOME%

REM ---------- [6/7] Disk space + prune dropped ABI artifacts ----------
REM Android + Gradle builds need several GB free. Prune emulator-only ABI
REM artifacts (we no longer build i686/x86_64) and refuse with guidance if low.
if exist "target\i686-linux-android" rmdir /s /q "target\i686-linux-android" >nul 2>nul
if exist "target\x86_64-linux-android" rmdir /s /q "target\x86_64-linux-android" >nul 2>nul
node scripts\check-disk.mjs 8
if errorlevel 1 (
  pause
  exit /b 1
)

REM ---------- [7/7] Build debug APK (auto-signed, installs immediately) ----------
REM Device ABIs only: aarch64 = all modern phones, armv7 = old 32-bit phones.
REM i686/x86_64 are emulator-only and their C toolchain regularly breaks
REM the build (sqlx archive failure) â€” CI still builds every ABI for release.
echo.
echo [BUILD] npx tauri android build --apk --debug -t aarch64 armv7
echo         First build takes several minutes (Rust + Gradle). Be patient.
echo.
call npx tauri android build --apk --debug -t aarch64 armv7
if errorlevel 1 (
  echo.
  echo [FATAL] Build failed â€” scroll up for the Gradle/Rust error.
  pause
  exit /b 1
)

echo.
echo  ============================================================
echo   SUCCESS â€” install-ready APK:
for /r "src-tauri\gen\android\app\build\outputs\apk" %%f in (*debug*.apk) do echo     %%f
echo.
echo   Install via USB ^(phone in developer-mode^):
echo     "%%ANDROID_HOME%%\platform-tools\adb.exe" install -r ^<apk-path^>
echo  ============================================================
pause
```

### `crates/pos-core/src/math.rs`

```rust
use crate::models::CartItem;

/// Calculates line item net total: (price * quantity) - discount
pub fn calculate_line_item_total(item: &CartItem) -> i64 {
    let gross = item.applied_price.saturating_mul(item.quantity);
    gross.saturating_sub(item.discount).max(0)
}

/// Calculates entire cart totals: (subtotal, total_discount, net_total)
pub fn calculate_cart_totals(items: &[CartItem]) -> (i64, i64, i64) {
    let mut subtotal: i64 = 0;
    let mut total_discount: i64 = 0;

    for item in items {
        let line_gross = item.applied_price.saturating_mul(item.quantity);
        subtotal = subtotal.saturating_add(line_gross);
        total_discount = total_discount.saturating_add(item.discount);
    }

    let net_total = subtotal.saturating_sub(total_discount).max(0);
    (subtotal, total_discount, net_total)
}

/// Computes expected profit: net_total - total_cost
pub fn calculate_gross_profit(items: &[CartItem]) -> i64 {
    let (_, _, net_total) = calculate_cart_totals(items);
    let total_cost: i64 = items
        .iter()
        .map(|it| it.cost_price.saturating_mul(it.quantity))
        .sum();
    net_total.saturating_sub(total_cost)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn test_cart_totals_and_profit() {
        let items = vec![
            CartItem {
                product_id: "prod-1".into(),
                quantity: 2,
                applied_price: 2500, // 2 * 2500 = 5000
                discount: 500,       // net = 4500
                cost_price: 1500,    // cost = 3000
                imei: None,
            },
            CartItem {
                product_id: "prod-2".into(),
                quantity: 1,
                applied_price: 1200,
                discount: 0,
                cost_price: 800,
                imei: None,
            },
        ];

        let (subtotal, discount, net) = calculate_cart_totals(&items);
        assert_eq!(subtotal, 6200);
        assert_eq!(discount, 500);
        assert_eq!(net, 5700);

        let profit = calculate_gross_profit(&items);
        assert_eq!(profit, 5700 - (3000 + 800)); // 1900
    }
}
```

pub struct Product {

    pub stock: i64,
    pub is_serialized: bool,
    pub reorder_point: i64,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct CartItem {

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq, Eq)]

use crate::error::PosError;
use crate::models::{LedgerDelta, OutboxRow, Product, SaleTransaction};

/// Universal PosDb trait unifying local terminal SQLite and Turso Cloud sync.
/// Implements AGENTS.md Â§1 Decision 4 & Â§6.1.
pub trait PosDb: Send + Sync {
    /// Retrieve product by ID
    fn get_product(&self, id: &str) -> Result<Option<Product>, PosError>;

    /// Retrieve all active catalog products
    fn get_all_products(&self) -> Result<Vec<Product>, PosError>;

    /// Atomic product upsert + ledger adjust recording
    fn upsert_product(&self, product: &Product) -> Result<(), PosError>;

    /// Process atomic sale: record sale, deduct ledger deltas, enqueue outbox
    fn record_sale(
        &self,
        sale: &SaleTransaction,
        deltas: &[LedgerDelta],
    ) -> Result<(), PosError>;

    /// Read pending mutations from the sync outbox
    fn get_pending_outbox(&self, limit: usize) -> Result<Vec<OutboxRow>, PosError>;

    /// Mark an outbox mutation as synced or inflight
    fn mark_outbox_status(
        &self,
        idempotency_key: &str,
        status: &str,
    ) -> Result<(), PosError>;
}
```
